title.en: Area: covering a region with tiles

text.en: Preetha covers her table with triangles and circles, Adrit with squares and rectangles. Whose shapes cover it without gaps? Area is how much surface a shape covers.

The region covered is called its area. We find area by filling a region with shapes that tile - no gaps and no overlaps - like squares, rectangles and triangles. Circles leave gaps.
Table 1 may take some number of triangles, Table 3 some squares and Table 4 some rectangles. The area is that count, in triangle units, square units or rectangle units.
To compare areas of rectangles A, B, C, trace and cut them, or place them on a square grid and count the squares.
We choose the square as the standard unit because its sides are equal. The area of a square with side 1 unit is 1 square unit; with side 1 cm it is 1 sq cm.
Compare two gardens on a grid by counting the squares each covers. Half squares are counted together to make whole ones.
Trace your palm or a leaf on a square grid and count whole and partly covered squares to estimate its area.
A rug made of square patches: count the patches in one row, then multiply by the rows.

problem.en: A rug has 5 rows with 6 square patches in each row. How many patches does it have?

text.en: Each row has 6 patches and there are 5 rows.
6 x 5 = 30 patches, so its area is 30 square units.

why.en: Count of unit squares is the area.

prompt.en: Why do we use a square as a unit of area?

requiredIdeas.en: All sides of a square are equal

points.en: Area is the surface a shape covers.
Tiles must leave no gaps and no overlaps.
The unit of area is a square unit.
Count squares on a grid to compare areas.
